title: Group medical visits compared with individual reviews for adults with type 2 diabetes
subtitle: Effectiveness question from a general practice; practice size, resources and timeframe not stated
statement: A general practice runs group visits for adults with type 2 diabetes and wants to know whether they achieve better results than individual reviews before expanding them. The need does not state how many patients, clinicians or practices could take part, which outcomes matter most to the partners, the timeframe or any funding; these are recorded as unknowns.
whoAffected: Adults with type 2 diabetes registered with the practice, particularly those above their HbA1c target; the nurses and GPs who run reviews; the partners deciding whether to expand group visits.
whatHurts: Poorly controlled diabetes leads to complications; expanding group visits that work no better than individual reviews would use clinic time without benefit, and patients who cannot attend groups could be disadvantaged.
currentPractice: Group visits are offered to some patients alongside usual individual reviews; outcomes have not been compared.
whyNow: The partners are considering expanding group visits and want evidence of effect first.
patientCenteredGoal: Adults with type 2 diabetes get the review format that best helps them manage their diabetes and that fits their lives.
summary: Problem framed as an effectiveness question; missing details are listed rather than assumed, and the design is left open.
